title: FlashAttention v3 buffer handoff: late-buffer scheduling & prefill tail-latency investigation
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Summary: After rolling FlashAttention v3 into the hosted serving runtime, we see intermittent tail-latency regressions (+12-18% P95 for short-sequence prefill workloads) attributed to delayed buffer reclamation and late allocations when multi-tenant kernels are scheduled back-to-back. The regression is most visible on bursty small-sequence chat traffic and on GPUs with tight device memory (A100 40GB shared pools).

Goals: 1) Reproduce reliably in microbench and CI; 2) Identify root cause (allocator interactions, CUDA stream ordering, kernel launch stalls, or v3 internal buffering changes); 3) Propose and implement mitigations with measurable improvement; 4) Roll out change via canary and monitor key metrics.

Observations/Signals: - P95 token decode latency for short sequences (<=64) increased from ~18ms to ~21.5ms on canary (12.8% regression) after v3 deployment. - Prefill latency spike correlates with GPU memory transient peaks and GPU kernel launch queues showing short bursts of >50ms stalls. - Heap fragmentation on the per-device custom allocator increases at high concurrency; counters show delayed free() completions. - v3 introduces larger per-kernel temporary buffers for certain tiling strategies which increases peak memory footprint and increases the number of allocation/free ops in decode-ready paths. - When the runtime switches from a prefill-heavy to decode-heavy workload (common in chat handoffs), we observe 'late buffers' that are freed but not immediately reusable by subsequent kernels on different CUDA streams due to stream synchronization semantics.

Repro steps (microbench): 1) Start multi-tenant local harness with 8 concurrent connections, A100-40, pool size 4. 2) Run prefill-only traffic 1000 requests of seq_len 64, then switch to 8x decode-heavy short messages. 3) Measure per-request P50/P95 and GPU allocator call latency with debug flags. Expected: see P95 spike within first 200 decode requests.

Immediate mitigations tried: - Turned on eager free batching (reduces amortized allocator overhead) -> P95 improved by ~4%. - Increased reserved buffer pool for short-seq fast-path -> eliminates most allocation stalls but increases memory pressure and fails under some Dedicated configs. - Fallback to FlashAttention v2 for short sequences on affected hosts -> restores pre-regression latency but reduces throughput by ~6% on long sequences.

Proposed options: A) Scoped allocator pool per-stream with lightweight lock-free freelist and eager reclamation (medium risk, medium engineering cost). B) Pre-warm kernel buffer pool at startup with size tuned by observed sequence histogram (low risk, increases steady-state memory). C) Add stream-aware buffer handoff semantics: when freeing on stream A, mark as immediately available for other streams via CUDA IPC-friendly pool (higher complexity). D) Short-sequence runtime fast-path that pins v2 kernels for seq<=64 until allocator improvements land (lowest code churn but multiplies code paths).

Plan: 1) Implement microbench instrumentation and record detailed allocator traces (ETA 2 days). 2) Prototype option B (pre-warm pool) in serving runtime and run canary on a dedicated subset (ETA 3 days). 3) Parallel spike: design lock-free per-stream freelist (option A) as longer-term fix (ETA 2 weeks). 4) If canary fails, fall back to v2 short-seq fast-path as temporary rollback (immediate).

Acceptance criteria: - P95 for short-seq prefill/first-decode within +3% of baseline (pre-v3) on canary hosts; - No increase in OOM incidents for Dedicated pools; - Stable allocator metrics (free latency stddev <5ms during bursts).
